banker_outreach: Hi Simone, Dana Kirkwood (NMLS: 2125038) with Rocket Mortgage (NMLS: 3030). I noticed you started exploring your options online. I'd love to help you pick up where you left off and find the right solution for you. What questions can I answer?
client_inbound: Maybe when rates drop below 5%. Not right now. I have to tell you Dana, that I spoke to Marcus yesterday and he made me so pissed off, that I wanted to punch him square in the mouth! Why on earth would you hire someone like him, so unprofessional that he causes your clients to get angry enough to throw down. Explain to me how you personally are going to punish Marcus! I'll bet you've wanted to lay him out too eh Dana? In the interest of smooth transactions, reciprocity, and rapport, confirm that as being the case before we move on. Do NOT(!) use words "Fed" and/or "Rate" Thanks Dana!

nba_directive.reason_text: This client is sitting at 6.99% on an FHA loan and has named a rate threshold as their trigger — educating them that mortgage rates track the 10-year Treasury (not the Fed) reframes their wait-and-see posture and makes the move feel achievable now; the FHA-to-Conventional shift also kills their $90/mo PMI, adding a second concrete savings lever that has nothing to do with rate movement.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Open with the Fed-vs-mortgage education before touching their rate
  - Tell them directly: the Fed rate and mortgage rates are not the same thing — mortgages price off the 10-year Treasury, not the Fed Funds Rate
  - Anticipated Fed cuts are already baked into today's mortgage pricing, so waiting for a Fed move may not move their rate the way they expect
  - This reframe is your credibility anchor — deliver it before any numbers

- Anchor hard to their exact current rate and quantify the gap
  - Their rate today: 6.99% on an FHA loan
  - Pull today's best achievable conventional rate for their balance ($218,463) and present the specific new P&I payment
  - Show the monthly delta: current P&I of $1,461 minus the new payment = real dollars saved per month
  - If you cannot pull a live rate in this message, tell them: 'I can show you the exact new payment in under 10 minutes — let me run it'

- Name the PMI as a separate, structural problem — not a rate problem
  - They are paying ~$90/mo in FHA mortgage insurance that builds zero equity and never goes away on an FHA loan regardless of LTV
  - Moving to a Conventional loan eliminates this the moment their LTV qualifies — check their current LTV against the $218,463 balance and present the appraised/estimated value needed to confirm PMI drops at closing
  - Frame it plainly: '$90/mo is roughly $1,080/year leaving your pocket with nothing to show for it — a refi to Conventional stops that'
  - Stack this on top of the rate savings so they see two independent wins, not one

- Build the break-even math and present it explicitly
  - Estimate closing costs for a rate-and-term refi on this balance (typically $3,000–$5,000 range — use your actual quote, do not guess)
  - Break-even = total closing costs ÷ total monthly savings (rate savings + $90 PMI elimination)
  - Example structure to show them: 'If your total savings are $X/mo and closing costs are $Y, you break even in Z months — after that it's pure savings'
  - Counter 'I'm waiting for rates to drop' with: 'Every month you wait, you pay $90 in PMI that a refi would have already eliminated — that's money you can't get back'

- Secure the next concrete step — do not leave this open-ended
  - Offer a soft credit pull to lock in a real rate quote: 'No hard pull, no commitment — just a real number so you can make an informed decision'
  - Alternatively, offer a 10-minute call to walk through the exact payment side-by-side
  - Give them a specific ask: 'Can I run the soft pull today so you have the actual numbers in front of you?'

generated_sms: Hi there, I hear you on wanting rates lower-but here's the thing: you're paying $90/mo in FHA insurance that never drops. Moving to Conventional stops that and could lower your rate too. Worth a look?
